tldr: In early September a startup and an academic paper both proposed giving AI agents persistent, shared memory instead of siloed per-session context. The pitch: context one agent learns should stay usable by every other agent on the same team, not vanish when a session ends.
whats_new: Motif open-sourced a shared, versioned memory store for teams of coding agents on Sept 21, following MemHub's commercial persistent-memory product and a kernel-managed-memory research paper earlier in the month.
why_it_matters: If cross-agent shared memory catches on, plan for memory-consistency and access-control problems, not just context loss — evaluate write conflicts before adopting a shared store.

beats.headline: MemHub ships persistent shared memory for coding agents
arXiv paper proposes kernel-managed shared memory for multi-agent personalization
Motif open-sources shared memory for teams of coding agents

open_questions: Does Motif or MemHub define a conflict-resolution model for concurrent agent writes to shared memory?
Does kernel-managed shared memory, the arXiv proposal, ship in any production agent framework, or does it remain research?
take_for_builders: Before adopting a shared-memory layer for a multi-agent team, test how it handles concurrent writes and stale reads — none of September's three releases publish a consistency model.
